problem.text: Sidorenko's inequality for even subdivisions of arbitrary graphs on Cayley hosts over finite abelian groups.

claims.text: Theorem 1.4: if each edge of an arbitrary graph is replaced by a path of even length, the resulting graph satisfies t(H, Cay(G,S)) >= t(K2, Cay(G,S))^{e(H)} for every finite abelian group G and symmetric S. Near-minimizing abelian Cayley hosts are spectrally quasirandom.

assumptions.text: The host is a Cayley graph over a finite abelian group; Szegedy's reduction (Proposition 1.2) needs Cayley hosts over all finite groups, so the abelian case is a restriction.

methods.text: The density is an average over the kernel of the circuit matrix (Proposition 2.3); Fourier expansion over the dual group; for a 1-subdivision the two Fourier coefficients on each subdivided edge are complex conjugates, so every term is nonnegative.

limitations.text: Only abelian Cayley hosts. The author states that the 1-subdivision question remains open for general hosts.

relevance.text: No result of this paper decides the statement or a declared neighbour. For the neighbours on 1-subdivisions (Conlon, Kim, Lee and Lee, Problem 1.5) and on the 1-subdivision S(H0) of the reported counterexample, it proves the inequality on Cayley hosts over finite abelian groups only, and it confirms that the general 1-subdivision question was open in July 2025. This record's inference, not a statement of the paper: the kernel of the reported counterexample is a difference kernel on an abelian group of matrices but also depends on type labels with their own activation laws, so it is not a Cayley host and Theorem 1.4 does not apply to it as stated.
